newsitem.title: USA: ComEd shutting Quad Cities 1 for 3-4 days.
newsitem.headline: ComEd shutting Quad Cities 1 for 3-4 days.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co is shutting its 789 megawatt (MW) Quad Cities 1 nuclear power plant for three to four days, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday.
The unit, in Cordova, Ill., was at 60 percent of its rated capacity early Tuesday and coasting down to a cold shutdown, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
A ComEd spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
Six of ComEd's 12 nuclear power units in Illinois, including Quad Cities 1, are now out of service, for a combined total generation capacity of 5,814 MW.
The 1,078 MW LaSalle unit 1 in Seneca, Ill., has been shut since September, 1996 for a maintenance outage and is tentatively scheduled to return to service in mid-April.
The adjacent 1,078 MW LaSalle unit 2 has been shut since September, 1996 for a maintenance and refueling outage, with no restart date set.
The 789 MW Quad Cities unit 2, also in Cordova, has been shut since March 1 for scheduled refueling and maintenance and is expected to return to service in early May.
Also, the 1,040 MW Zion unit 1 in Zion, Ill., has been shut since late February for repairs to a diesel generator, and is expected to return to service in early May.
The adjoining 1,040 MW Zion unit 2 has been shut since September, 1996 for refueling and is expected to return to service in mid-April.
As of early Tuesday, several ComEd nuclear units were also operating at a reduced power level, the NRC said.
The 794 MW Dresden unit 3 was operating at 66 percent of capacity early Tuesday as it coasts down to a refueling outage set to begin March 30, the NRC said.
The 1,105 Byron unit 2 in Byron, Ill., was operating at 68 percent as of early Tuesday and was reducing to 50 percent of output to correct a secondary system chemistry problem, the NRC said.
